simple.meaning: מַלְקוֹשׁ (malqôwsh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “the spring rain ; figuratively, eloquence.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Deuteronomy 11:14. The surrounding context includes family line, kingship, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַלְקוֹשׁ (H4456) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מַלְקוֹשׁ (malqôwsh) / H4456 is traced through Deuteronomy 11:14, Job 29:23, Proverbs 16:15, Jeremiah 3:3 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: that I will give the rain for your land in its season, the early rain and the latter rain, that you may gather in your grain, your new wine, and your oil.
They waited for me as for the rain.
In the light of the king’s face is life.

They don’t say in their heart, ‘Let’s now fear Yahweh our God, who gives rain, both the former and the latter, in its season, who preserves to us the appointed weeks of the harvest.’

definitions.full: H4456. malqosh מַלְקוֺשׁ noun masculine Jer 3:3 latter-rain, spring-rain (i.e. showers of March-April; important, as strengthening and maturing crops); ׳מ Hosea 6:3 7 t.; — related to גֶּשֶׁם as particular to General, opposed to יוֺרֶה ( former rain , q. v.): 6:3 ; Jer 5:24 ; so opposed to מוֺרֶה Joel 2:23 ; particular under מָטָר Deut 11:14 (opposed to יוֺרֶה ), Zech 10:1 (+ מְטַרגֶּֿשֶׁם ), Job 29:23 ; || רְבִבִים Jer 3:3 ; מ ׳עָב Prov 16:15 spring-rain-cloud (simile of king's favour).
